observations:
Torah #72 is a tightly focused teaching on a single domain: the taxonomy of the evil inclination (yetzer hara) across its multiple levels of manifestation. All bechina-connected nodes in the dataset (6 nodes across 3 edges), all gap additions flagged in torah_72_additions.json (3 concepts: דם שבחלל השמאלי, קליפה דקה, כתר עליון אוכמא), and all other bechina-language concepts examined fall within one and only one conceptual domain — the yetzer hara in its levels.

The Torah's entire structure is a single conceptual taxonomy moving from: (1) the lowest physical level — turbid blood, shtut, dimyonot, hirhurei znut = avodah zarah = elilim; through (2) the intermediate level — klipa daka; up to (3) the upper spiritual level — gevurot, dinim, midas hadin; and finally to (4) the cosmic/divine level — keter elyon okhama relative to the Ain Sof. This is one package, not multiple, because the Rebbe explicitly presents all levels as aspects of the same phenomenon ('yesh kama bechinot b'yetzer hara') and connects them all through a single root (midas hadin).

The positive side of the teaching — teshuvah, the tzaddik, bodily purity, sweetening the dinim — is presented entirely in eitza terms (cause-and-effect chains describing what one must DO and what RESULTS). No positive conceptual cluster receives bechina-language declarations in this Torah. Concepts like 'chacham ha'emet', 'taharas haguf', 'da'at' and 'teshuvah' appear as instrumental/causal actors (eitza), not as bechina-equivalent nodes forming a good-polarity package.

Therefore: no new package is warranted. The single package יֵצֶר הָרָע fully accounts for all bechina-identified conceptual content in Torah #72.
